clauses.normalized_text: This document describes loss detection and congestion control mechanisms for QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: This document describes loss detection and congestion control mechanisms for QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC is a new multiplexed and secure transport atop UDP.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC is a new multiplexed and secure transport atop UDP.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC builds on decades of transport and security experience, and implements mechanisms that make it attractive as a modern general-purpose transport.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC builds on decades of transport and security experience, and implements mechanisms that make it attractive as a modern general-purpose transport.

clauses.normalized_text: The QUIC protocol is described in [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
clauses.raw_text: The QUIC protocol is described in [QUIC-TRANSPORT].

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implements the spirit of known TCP loss recovery mechanisms, described in RFCs, various Internet-drafts, and also those prevalent in the Linux TCP implementation.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implements the spirit of known TCP loss recovery mechanisms, described in RFCs, various Internet-drafts, and also those prevalent in the Linux TCP implementation.

clauses.normalized_text: This document describes QUIC congestion control and loss recovery, and where applicable, attributes the TCP equivalent in RFCs, Internet-drafts, academic papers, and/or TCP implementations.
clauses.raw_text: This document describes QUIC congestion control and loss recovery, and where applicable, attributes the TCP equivalent in RFCs, Internet-drafts, academic papers, and/or TCP implementations.

clauses.normalized_text: The key words “MUST”, “MUST NOT”, “REQUIRED”, “SHALL”, “SHALL NOT”, “SHOULD”, “SHOULD NOT”, “RECOMMENDED”, “NOT RECOMMENDED”, “MAY”, and “OPTIONAL” in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
clauses.raw_text: The key words “MUST”, “MUST NOT”, “REQUIRED”, “SHALL”, “SHALL NOT”, “SHOULD”, “SHOULD NOT”, “RECOMMENDED”, “NOT RECOMMENDED”, “MAY”, and “OPTIONAL” in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

clauses.normalized_text: All transmissions in QUIC are sent with a packet-level header, which includes a packet sequence number (referred to below as a packet number).
clauses.raw_text: All transmissions in QUIC are sent with a packet-level header, which includes a packet sequence number (referred to below as a packet number).
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: These packet numbers never repeat in the lifetime of a connection, and are monotonically increasing, which prevents ambiguity.
clauses.raw_text: These packet numbers never repeat in the lifetime of a connection, and are monotonically increasing, which prevents ambiguity.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: This fundamental design decision obviates the need for disambiguating between transmissions and retransmissions and eliminates significant complexity from QUIC’s interpretation of TCP loss detection mechanisms.
clauses.raw_text: This fundamental design decision obviates the need for disambiguating between transmissions and retransmissions and eliminates significant complexity from QUIC’s interpretation of TCP loss detection mechanisms.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: Every packet may contain several frames.
clauses.raw_text: Every packet may contain several frames.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: We outline the frames that are important to the loss detection and congestion control machinery below.
clauses.raw_text: We outline the frames that are important to the loss detection and congestion control machinery below.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: Retransmittable frames are frames requiring reliable delivery.
clauses.raw_text: Retransmittable frames are frames requiring reliable delivery.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: The most common are STREAM frames, which typically contain application data.
clauses.raw_text: The most common are STREAM frames, which typically contain application data.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: Crypto handshake data is sent on stream 0, and uses the reliability machinery of QUIC underneath.
clauses.raw_text: Crypto handshake data is sent on stream 0, and uses the reliability machinery of QUIC underneath.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: ACK frames contain acknowledgment information.
clauses.raw_text: ACK frames contain acknowledgment information.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: ACK frames contain one or more ranges of acknowledged packets.
clauses.raw_text: ACK frames contain one or more ranges of acknowledged packets.
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: Readers familiar with TCP’s loss detection and congestion control will find algorithms here that parallel well-known TCP ones.
clauses.raw_text: Readers familiar with TCP’s loss detection and congestion control will find algorithms here that parallel well-known TCP ones.
clauses.section_heading: Relevant Differences Between QUIC and TCP

clauses.normalized_text: Protocol differences between QUIC and TCP however contribute to algorithmic differences.
clauses.raw_text: Protocol differences between QUIC and TCP however contribute to algorithmic differences.
clauses.section_heading: Relevant Differences Between QUIC and TCP

clauses.normalized_text: We briefly describe these protocol differences below.
clauses.raw_text: We briefly describe these protocol differences below.
clauses.section_heading: Relevant Differences Between QUIC and TCP

clauses.normalized_text: TCP conflates transmission sequence number at the sender with delivery sequence number at the receiver, which results in retransmissions of the same data carrying the same sequence number, and consequently to problems caused by “retransmission ambiguity”.
clauses.raw_text: TCP conflates transmission sequence number at the sender with delivery sequence number at the receiver, which results in retransmissions of the same data carrying the same sequence number, and consequently to problems caused by “retransmission ambiguity”.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC separates the two: QUIC uses a packet number for transmissions, and any data that is to be delivered to the receiving application(s) is sent in one or more streams, with delivery order determined by stream offsets encoded within STREAM frames.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC separates the two: QUIC uses a packet number for transmissions, and any data that is to be delivered to the receiving application(s) is sent in one or more streams, with delivery order determined by stream offsets encoded within STREAM frames.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC’s packet number is strictly increasing, and directly encodes transmission order.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC’s packet number is strictly increasing, and directly encodes transmission order.

clauses.normalized_text: A higher QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent later, and a lower QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent earlier.
clauses.raw_text: A higher QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent later, and a lower QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent earlier.

clauses.normalized_text: When a packet containing frames is deemed lost, QUIC rebundles necessary frames in a new packet with a new packet number, removing ambiguity about which packet is acknowledged when an ACK is received.
clauses.raw_text: When a packet containing frames is deemed lost, QUIC rebundles necessary frames in a new packet with a new packet number, removing ambiguity about which packet is acknowledged when an ACK is received.

clauses.normalized_text: Consequently, more accurate RTT measurements can be made, spurious retransmissions are trivially detected, and mechanisms such as Fast Retransmit can be applied universally, based only on packet number.
clauses.raw_text: Consequently, more accurate RTT measurements can be made, spurious retransmissions are trivially detected, and mechanisms such as Fast Retransmit can be applied universally, based only on packet number.

clauses.normalized_text: This design point significantly simplifies loss detection mechanisms for QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: This design point significantly simplifies loss detection mechanisms for QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: Most TCP mechanisms implicitly attempt to infer transmission ordering based on TCP sequence numbers - a non-trivial task, especially when TCP timestamps are not available.
clauses.raw_text: Most TCP mechanisms implicitly attempt to infer transmission ordering based on TCP sequence numbers - a non-trivial task, especially when TCP timestamps are not available.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC ACKs contain information that is similar to TCP SACK, but QUIC does not allow any acked packet to be reneged, greatly simplifying implementations on both sides and reducing memory pressure on the sender.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC ACKs contain information that is similar to TCP SACK, but QUIC does not allow any acked packet to be reneged, greatly simplifying implementations on both sides and reducing memory pressure on the sender.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC supports many ACK ranges, opposed to TCP’s 3 SACK ranges.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC supports many ACK ranges, opposed to TCP’s 3 SACK ranges.

clauses.normalized_text: In high loss environments, this speeds recovery, reduces spurious retransmits, and ensures forward progress without relying on timeouts.
clauses.raw_text: In high loss environments, this speeds recovery, reduces spurious retransmits, and ensures forward progress without relying on timeouts.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC ACKs explicitly encode the delay incurred at the receiver between when a packet is received and when the corresponding ACK is sent.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC ACKs explicitly encode the delay incurred at the receiver between when a packet is received and when the corresponding ACK is sent.

clauses.normalized_text: This allows the receiver of the ACK to adjust for receiver delays, specifically the delayed ack timer, when estimating the path RTT.
clauses.raw_text: This allows the receiver of the ACK to adjust for receiver delays, specifically the delayed ack timer, when estimating the path RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: This mechanism also allows a receiver to measure and report the delay from when a packet was received by the OS kernel, which is useful in receivers which may incur delays such as context-switch latency before a userspace QUIC receiver processes a received packet.
clauses.raw_text: This mechanism also allows a receiver to measure and report the delay from when a packet was received by the OS kernel, which is useful in receivers which may incur delays such as context-switch latency before a userspace QUIC receiver processes a received packet.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC senders use both ack information and timeouts to detect lost packets, and this section provides a description of these algorithms.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC senders use both ack information and timeouts to detect lost packets, and this section provides a description of these algorithms.

clauses.normalized_text: Estimating the network round-trip time (RTT) is critical to these algorithms and is described first.
clauses.raw_text: Estimating the network round-trip time (RTT) is critical to these algorithms and is described first.

clauses.normalized_text: RTT is calculated when an ACK frame arrives by computing the difference between the current time and the time the largest newly acked packet was sent.
clauses.raw_text: RTT is calculated when an ACK frame arrives by computing the difference between the current time and the time the largest newly acked packet was sent.

clauses.normalized_text: If no packets are newly acknowledged, RTT cannot be calculated. When RTT is calculated, the ack delay field from the ACK frame SHOULD be subtracted from the RTT as long as the result is larger than the Min RTT.
clauses.raw_text: If no packets are newly acknowledged, RTT cannot be calculated. When RTT is calculated, the ack delay field from the ACK frame SHOULD be subtracted from the RTT as long as the result is larger than the Min RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: If the result is smaller than the min_rtt, the RTT should be used, but the ack delay field should be ignored.
clauses.raw_text: If the result is smaller than the min_rtt, the RTT should be used, but the ack delay field should be ignored.

clauses.normalized_text: Like TCP, QUIC calculates both smoothed RTT and RTT variance as specified in [RFC6298].
clauses.raw_text: Like TCP, QUIC calculates both smoothed RTT and RTT variance as specified in [RFC6298].

clauses.normalized_text: Min RTT is the minimum RTT measured over the connection, prior to adjusting by ack delay.
clauses.raw_text: Min RTT is the minimum RTT measured over the connection, prior to adjusting by ack delay.

clauses.normalized_text: Ignoring ack delay for min RTT prevents intentional or unintentional underestimation of min RTT, which in turn prevents underestimating smoothed RTT.
clauses.raw_text: Ignoring ack delay for min RTT prevents intentional or unintentional underestimation of min RTT, which in turn prevents underestimating smoothed RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: Ack-based loss detection implements the spirit of TCP’s Fast Retransmit [RFC5681], Early Retransmit [RFC5827], FACK, and SACK loss recovery [RFC6675].
clauses.raw_text: Ack-based loss detection implements the spirit of TCP’s Fast Retransmit [RFC5681], Early Retransmit [RFC5827], FACK, and SACK loss recovery [RFC6675].

clauses.normalized_text: This section provides an overview of how these algorithms are implemented in QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: This section provides an overview of how these algorithms are implemented in QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: (TODO: Define unacknowledged packet, ackable packet, outstanding bytes.)
clauses.raw_text: (TODO: Define unacknowledged packet, ackable packet, outstanding bytes.)

clauses.normalized_text: An unacknowledged packet is marked as lost when an acknowledgment is received for a packet that was sent a threshold number of packets (kReorderingThreshold) after the unacknowledged packet.
clauses.raw_text: An unacknowledged packet is marked as lost when an acknowledgment is received for a packet that was sent a threshold number of packets (kReorderingThreshold) after the unacknowledged packet.

clauses.normalized_text: Receipt of the ack indicates that a later packet was received, while kReorderingThreshold provides some tolerance for reordering of packets in the network.
clauses.raw_text: Receipt of the ack indicates that a later packet was received, while kReorderingThreshold provides some tolerance for reordering of packets in the network.

clauses.normalized_text: The RECOMMENDED initial value for kReorderingThreshold is 3.
clauses.raw_text: The RECOMMENDED initial value for kReorderingThreshold is 3.

clauses.normalized_text: We derive this default from recommendations for TCP loss recovery [RFC5681] [RFC6675].
clauses.raw_text: We derive this default from recommendations for TCP loss recovery [RFC5681] [RFC6675].

clauses.normalized_text: It is possible for networks to exhibit higher degrees of reordering, causing a sender to detect spurious losses.
clauses.raw_text: It is possible for networks to exhibit higher degrees of reordering, causing a sender to detect spurious losses.

clauses.normalized_text: Detecting spurious losses leads to unnecessary retransmissions and may result in degraded performance due to the actions of the congestion controller upon detecting loss.
clauses.raw_text: Detecting spurious losses leads to unnecessary retransmissions and may result in degraded performance due to the actions of the congestion controller upon detecting loss.

clauses.normalized_text: Implementers MAY use algorithms developed for TCP, such as TCP-NCR [RFC4653], to improve QUIC’s reordering resilience, though care should be taken to map TCP specifics to QUIC correctly.
clauses.raw_text: Implementers MAY use algorithms developed for TCP, such as TCP-NCR [RFC4653], to improve QUIC’s reordering resilience, though care should be taken to map TCP specifics to QUIC correctly.

clauses.normalized_text: Similarly, using time-based loss detection to deal with reordering, such as in PR-TCP, should be more readily usable in QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: Similarly, using time-based loss detection to deal with reordering, such as in PR-TCP, should be more readily usable in QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: Making QUIC deal with such networks is important open research, and implementers are encouraged to explore this space.
clauses.raw_text: Making QUIC deal with such networks is important open research, and implementers are encouraged to explore this space.

clauses.normalized_text: Unacknowledged packets close to the tail may have fewer than kReorderingThreshold number of ackable packets sent after them.
clauses.raw_text: Unacknowledged packets close to the tail may have fewer than kReorderingThreshold number of ackable packets sent after them.

clauses.normalized_text: Loss of such packets cannot be detected via Fast Retransmit.
clauses.raw_text: Loss of such packets cannot be detected via Fast Retransmit.

clauses.normalized_text: To enable ack-based loss detection of such packets, receipt of an acknowledgment for the last outstanding ackable packet triggers the Early Retransmit process, as follows.
clauses.raw_text: To enable ack-based loss detection of such packets, receipt of an acknowledgment for the last outstanding ackable packet triggers the Early Retransmit process, as follows.

clauses.normalized_text: If there are unacknowledged ackable packets still pending, they ought to be marked as lost. To compensate for the reduced reordering resilience, the sender SHOULD set an alarm for a small period of time.
clauses.raw_text: If there are unacknowledged ackable packets still pending, they ought to be marked as lost. To compensate for the reduced reordering resilience, the sender SHOULD set an alarm for a small period of time.

clauses.normalized_text: If the unacknowledged ackable packets are not acknowledged during this time, then these packets MUST be marked as lost.
clauses.raw_text: If the unacknowledged ackable packets are not acknowledged during this time, then these packets MUST be marked as lost.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint SHOULD set the alarm such that a packet is marked as lost no earlier than 1.25 * max(SRTT, latest_RTT) since when it was sent.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint SHOULD set the alarm such that a packet is marked as lost no earlier than 1.25 * max(SRTT, latest_RTT) since when it was sent.

clauses.normalized_text: Using max(SRTT, latest_RTT) protects from the two following cases:
clauses.raw_text: Using max(SRTT, latest_RTT) protects from the two following cases:

clauses.normalized_text: the latest RTT sample is lower than the SRTT, perhaps due to reordering where packet whose ack triggered the Early Retransit process encountered a shorter path;
clauses.raw_text: the latest RTT sample is lower than the SRTT, perhaps due to reordering where packet whose ack triggered the Early Retransit process encountered a shorter path;

clauses.normalized_text: the latest RTT sample is higher than the SRTT, perhaps due to a sustained increase in the actual RTT, but the smoothed SRTT has not yet caught up.
clauses.raw_text: the latest RTT sample is higher than the SRTT, perhaps due to a sustained increase in the actual RTT, but the smoothed SRTT has not yet caught up.

clauses.normalized_text: The 1.25 multiplier increases reordering resilience.
clauses.raw_text: The 1.25 multiplier increases reordering resilience.

clauses.normalized_text: Implementers MAY experiment with using other multipliers, bearing in mind that a lower multiplier reduces reordering resilience and increases spurious retransmissions, and a higher multipler increases loss recovery delay.
clauses.raw_text: Implementers MAY experiment with using other multipliers, bearing in mind that a lower multiplier reduces reordering resilience and increases spurious retransmissions, and a higher multipler increases loss recovery delay.

clauses.normalized_text: This mechanism is based on Early Retransmit for TCP [RFC5827].
clauses.raw_text: This mechanism is based on Early Retransmit for TCP [RFC5827].

clauses.normalized_text: However, [RFC5827] does not include the alarm described above.
clauses.raw_text: However, [RFC5827] does not include the alarm described above.

clauses.normalized_text: Early Retransmit is prone to spurious retransmissions due to its reduced reordering resilence without the alarm.
clauses.raw_text: Early Retransmit is prone to spurious retransmissions due to its reduced reordering resilence without the alarm.

clauses.normalized_text: This observation led Linux TCP implementers to implement an alarm for TCP as well, and this document incorporates this advancement.
clauses.raw_text: This observation led Linux TCP implementers to implement an alarm for TCP as well, and this document incorporates this advancement.

clauses.normalized_text: Timer-based loss detection implements the spirit of TCP’s Tail Loss Probe and Retransmission Timeout mechanisms.
clauses.raw_text: Timer-based loss detection implements the spirit of TCP’s Tail Loss Probe and Retransmission Timeout mechanisms.

clauses.normalized_text: The algorithm described in this section is an adaptation of the Tail Loss Probe algorithm proposed for TCP [TLP].
clauses.raw_text: The algorithm described in this section is an adaptation of the Tail Loss Probe algorithm proposed for TCP [TLP].

clauses.normalized_text: A packet sent at the tail is particularly vulnerable to slow loss detection, since acks of subsequent packets are needed to trigger ack-based detection.
clauses.raw_text: A packet sent at the tail is particularly vulnerable to slow loss detection, since acks of subsequent packets are needed to trigger ack-based detection.

clauses.normalized_text: To ameliorate this weakness of tail packets, the sender schedules an alarm when the last ackable packet before quiescence is transmitted.
clauses.raw_text: To ameliorate this weakness of tail packets, the sender schedules an alarm when the last ackable packet before quiescence is transmitted.

clauses.normalized_text: When this alarm fires, a Tail Loss Probe (TLP) packet is sent to evoke an acknowledgement from the receiver.
clauses.raw_text: When this alarm fires, a Tail Loss Probe (TLP) packet is sent to evoke an acknowledgement from the receiver.

clauses.normalized_text: The alarm duration, or Probe Timeout (PTO), is set based on the following conditions:
clauses.raw_text: The alarm duration, or Probe Timeout (PTO), is set based on the following conditions:

clauses.normalized_text: PTO SHOULD be scheduled for max(1.5*SRTT+MaxAckDelay, 10ms)
clauses.raw_text: PTO SHOULD be scheduled for max(1.5*SRTT+MaxAckDelay, 10ms)

clauses.normalized_text: If RTO ([rto]) is earlier, schedule a TLP alarm in its place. That is, PTO SHOULD be scheduled for min(RTO, PTO).
clauses.raw_text: If RTO ([rto]) is earlier, schedule a TLP alarm in its place. That is, PTO SHOULD be scheduled for min(RTO, PTO).

clauses.normalized_text: MaxAckDelay is the maximum ack delay supplied in an incoming ACK frame.
clauses.raw_text: MaxAckDelay is the maximum ack delay supplied in an incoming ACK frame.

clauses.normalized_text: MaxAckDelay excludes ack delays that aren’t included in an RTT sample because they’re too large and excludes those which reference an ack-only packet.
clauses.raw_text: MaxAckDelay excludes ack delays that aren’t included in an RTT sample because they’re too large and excludes those which reference an ack-only packet.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC diverges from TCP by calculating MaxAckDelay dynamically, instead of assuming a constant delayed ack timeout for all connections.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC diverges from TCP by calculating MaxAckDelay dynamically, instead of assuming a constant delayed ack timeout for all connections.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC includes this in all probe timeouts, because it assume the ack delay may come into play, regardless of the number of packets outstanding.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC includes this in all probe timeouts, because it assume the ack delay may come into play, regardless of the number of packets outstanding.

clauses.normalized_text: TCP’s TLP assumes if at least 2 packets are outstanding, acks will not be delayed.
clauses.raw_text: TCP’s TLP assumes if at least 2 packets are outstanding, acks will not be delayed.

clauses.normalized_text: A PTO value of at least 1.5*SRTT ensures that the ACK is overdue.
clauses.raw_text: A PTO value of at least 1.5*SRTT ensures that the ACK is overdue.

clauses.normalized_text: The 1.5 is based on [LOSS-PROBE], but implementations MAY experiment with other constants.
clauses.raw_text: The 1.5 is based on [LOSS-PROBE], but implementations MAY experiment with other constants.

clauses.normalized_text: To reduce latency, it is RECOMMENDED that the sender set and allow the TLP alarm to fire twice before setting an RTO alarm.
clauses.raw_text: To reduce latency, it is RECOMMENDED that the sender set and allow the TLP alarm to fire twice before setting an RTO alarm.

clauses.normalized_text: In other words, when the TLP alarm fires the first time, a TLP packet is sent, and it is RECOMMENDED that the TLP alarm be scheduled for a second time.
clauses.raw_text: In other words, when the TLP alarm fires the first time, a TLP packet is sent, and it is RECOMMENDED that the TLP alarm be scheduled for a second time.

clauses.normalized_text: When the TLP alarm fires the second time, a second TLP packet is sent, and an RTO alarm SHOULD be scheduled [rto].
clauses.raw_text: When the TLP alarm fires the second time, a second TLP packet is sent, and an RTO alarm SHOULD be scheduled [rto].

clauses.normalized_text: A TLP packet SHOULD carry new data when possible.
clauses.raw_text: A TLP packet SHOULD carry new data when possible.

clauses.normalized_text: If new data is unavailable or new data cannot be sent due to flow control, a TLP packet MAY retransmit unacknowledged data to potentially reduce recovery time.
clauses.raw_text: If new data is unavailable or new data cannot be sent due to flow control, a TLP packet MAY retransmit unacknowledged data to potentially reduce recovery time.

clauses.normalized_text: Since a TLP alarm is used to send a probe into the network prior to establishing any packet loss, prior unacknowledged packets SHOULD NOT be marked as lost when a TLP alarm fires.
clauses.raw_text: Since a TLP alarm is used to send a probe into the network prior to establishing any packet loss, prior unacknowledged packets SHOULD NOT be marked as lost when a TLP alarm fires.

clauses.normalized_text: A TLP packet MUST NOT be blocked by the sender’s congestion controller.
clauses.raw_text: A TLP packet MUST NOT be blocked by the sender’s congestion controller.

clauses.normalized_text: The sender MUST however count these bytes as additional bytes in flight, since a TLP adds network load without establishing packet loss.
clauses.raw_text: The sender MUST however count these bytes as additional bytes in flight, since a TLP adds network load without establishing packet loss.

clauses.normalized_text: A sender may not know that a packet being sent is a tail packet.
clauses.raw_text: A sender may not know that a packet being sent is a tail packet.

clauses.normalized_text: Consequently, a sender may have to arm or adjust the TLP alarm on every sent ackable packet.
clauses.raw_text: Consequently, a sender may have to arm or adjust the TLP alarm on every sent ackable packet.

clauses.normalized_text: A Retransmission Timeout (RTO) alarm is the final backstop for loss detection.
clauses.raw_text: A Retransmission Timeout (RTO) alarm is the final backstop for loss detection.

clauses.normalized_text: The algorithm used in QUIC is based on the RTO algorithm for TCP [RFC5681] and is additionally resilient to spurious RTO events [RFC5682].
clauses.raw_text: The algorithm used in QUIC is based on the RTO algorithm for TCP [RFC5681] and is additionally resilient to spurious RTO events [RFC5682].

clauses.normalized_text: When the last TLP packet is sent, an alarm is scheduled for the RTO period.
clauses.raw_text: When the last TLP packet is sent, an alarm is scheduled for the RTO period.

clauses.normalized_text: When this alarm fires, the sender sends two packets, to evoke acknowledgements from the receiver, and restarts the RTO alarm.
clauses.raw_text: When this alarm fires, the sender sends two packets, to evoke acknowledgements from the receiver, and restarts the RTO alarm.

clauses.normalized_text: Similar to TCP [RFC6298], the RTO period is set based on the following conditions:
clauses.raw_text: Similar to TCP [RFC6298], the RTO period is set based on the following conditions:

clauses.normalized_text: When the final TLP packet is sent, the RTO period is set to max(SRTT + 4*RTTVAR + MaxAckDelay, minRTO)
clauses.raw_text: When the final TLP packet is sent, the RTO period is set to max(SRTT + 4*RTTVAR + MaxAckDelay, minRTO)

clauses.normalized_text: When an RTO alarm fires, the RTO period is doubled.
clauses.raw_text: When an RTO alarm fires, the RTO period is doubled.

clauses.normalized_text: The sender typically has incurred a high latency penalty by the time an RTO alarm fires, and this penalty increases exponentially in subsequent consecutive RTO events.
clauses.raw_text: The sender typically has incurred a high latency penalty by the time an RTO alarm fires, and this penalty increases exponentially in subsequent consecutive RTO events.

clauses.normalized_text: Sending a single packet on an RTO event therefore makes the connection very sensitive to single packet loss.
clauses.raw_text: Sending a single packet on an RTO event therefore makes the connection very sensitive to single packet loss.

clauses.normalized_text: Sending two packets instead of one significantly increases resilience to packet drop in both directions, thus reducing the probability of consecutive RTO events.
clauses.raw_text: Sending two packets instead of one significantly increases resilience to packet drop in both directions, thus reducing the probability of consecutive RTO events.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC’s RTO algorithm differs from TCP in that the firing of an RTO alarm is not considered a strong enough signal of packet loss, so does not result in an immediate change to congestion window or recovery state.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC’s RTO algorithm differs from TCP in that the firing of an RTO alarm is not considered a strong enough signal of packet loss, so does not result in an immediate change to congestion window or recovery state.

clauses.normalized_text: An RTO alarm fires only when there’s a prolonged period of network silence, which could be caused by a change in the underlying network RTT.
clauses.raw_text: An RTO alarm fires only when there’s a prolonged period of network silence, which could be caused by a change in the underlying network RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC also diverges from TCP by including MaxAckDelay in the RTO period.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC also diverges from TCP by including MaxAckDelay in the RTO period.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC is able to explicitly model delay at the receiver via the ack delay field in the ACK frame.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC is able to explicitly model delay at the receiver via the ack delay field in the ACK frame.

clauses.normalized_text: Since QUIC corrects for this delay in its SRTT and RTTVAR computations, it is necessary to add this delay explicitly in the TLP and RTO computation.

OnPacketSent(packet_number, is_ack_only, sent_bytes):
  time_of_last_sent_packet = now
  largest_sent_packet = packet_number

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC loss detection uses a single alarm for all timer-based loss detection.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC loss detection uses a single alarm for all timer-based loss detection.

clauses.normalized_text: The duration of the alarm is based on the alarm’s mode, which is set in the packet and timer events further below.

clauses.normalized_text: The function SetLossDetectionAlarm defined below shows how the single timer is set based on the alarm mode.
clauses.raw_text: The function SetLossDetectionAlarm defined below shows how the single timer is set based on the alarm mode.

clauses.normalized_text: When a connection has unacknowledged handshake data, the handshake alarm is set and when it expires, all unacknowledgedd handshake data is retransmitted.
clauses.raw_text: When a connection has unacknowledged handshake data, the handshake alarm is set and when it expires, all unacknowledgedd handshake data is retransmitted.

clauses.normalized_text: When stateless rejects are in use, the connection is considered immediately closed once a reject is sent, so no timer is set to retransmit the reject.
clauses.raw_text: When stateless rejects are in use, the connection is considered immediately closed once a reject is sent, so no timer is set to retransmit the reject.

clauses.normalized_text: Version negotiation packets are always stateless, and MUST be sent once per handshake packet that uses an unsupported QUIC version, and MAY be sent in response to 0RTT packets.
clauses.raw_text: Version negotiation packets are always stateless, and MUST be sent once per handshake packet that uses an unsupported QUIC version, and MAY be sent in response to 0RTT packets.

clauses.normalized_text: Tail loss probes [LOSS-PROBE] and retransmission timeouts [RFC6298] are an alarm based mechanism to recover from cases when there are outstanding retransmittable packets, but an acknowledgement has not been received in a timely manner.
clauses.raw_text: Tail loss probes [LOSS-PROBE] and retransmission timeouts [RFC6298] are an alarm based mechanism to recover from cases when there are outstanding retransmittable packets, but an acknowledgement has not been received in a timely manner.

clauses.normalized_text: A shorter delayed ack time of 25ms was chosen because longer delayed acks can delay loss recovery and for the small number of connections where less than packet per 25ms is delivered, acking every packet is beneficial to congestion control and loss recovery.
clauses.raw_text: A shorter delayed ack time of 25ms was chosen because longer delayed acks can delay loss recovery and for the small number of connections where less than packet per 25ms is delivered, acking every packet is beneficial to congestion control and loss recovery.

clauses.normalized_text: The default initial RTT of 100ms was chosen because it is slightly higher than both the median and mean min_rtt typically observed on the public internet.
clauses.raw_text: The default initial RTT of 100ms was chosen because it is slightly higher than both the median and mean min_rtt typically observed on the public internet.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC’s congestion control is based on TCP NewReno[RFC6582] congestion control to determine the congestion window and pacing rate.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC’s congestion control is based on TCP NewReno[RFC6582] congestion control to determine the congestion window and pacing rate.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC congestion control is specified in bytes due to finer control and the ease of appropriate byte counting[RFC3465].
clauses.raw_text: QUIC congestion control is specified in bytes due to finer control and the ease of appropriate byte counting[RFC3465].

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC begins every connection in slow start and exits slow start upon loss.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC begins every connection in slow start and exits slow start upon loss.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC re-enters slow start anytime the congestion window is less than sshthresh, which typically only occurs after an RTO.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC re-enters slow start anytime the congestion window is less than sshthresh, which typically only occurs after an RTO.

clauses.normalized_text: While in slow start, QUIC increases the congestion window by the number of acknowledged bytes when each ack is processed.
clauses.raw_text: While in slow start, QUIC increases the congestion window by the number of acknowledged bytes when each ack is processed.

clauses.normalized_text: Slow start exits to congestion avoidance.
clauses.raw_text: Slow start exits to congestion avoidance.

clauses.normalized_text: Congestion avoidance in NewReno uses an additive increase multiplicative decrease (AIMD) approach that increases the congestion window by one MSS of bytes per congestion window acknowledged.
clauses.raw_text: Congestion avoidance in NewReno uses an additive increase multiplicative decrease (AIMD) approach that increases the congestion window by one MSS of bytes per congestion window acknowledged.

clauses.normalized_text: When a loss is detected, NewReno halves the congestion window and sets the slow start threshold to the new congestion window.
clauses.raw_text: When a loss is detected, NewReno halves the congestion window and sets the slow start threshold to the new congestion window.

clauses.normalized_text: Recovery is a period of time beginning with detection of a lost packet.
clauses.raw_text: Recovery is a period of time beginning with detection of a lost packet.

clauses.normalized_text: Because QUIC retransmits stream data and control frames, not packets, it defines the end of recovery as a packet sent after the start of recovery being acknowledged.
clauses.raw_text: Because QUIC retransmits stream data and control frames, not packets, it defines the end of recovery as a packet sent after the start of recovery being acknowledged.

clauses.normalized_text: This is slightly different from TCP’s definition of recovery ending when the lost packet that started recovery is acknowledged.
clauses.raw_text: This is slightly different from TCP’s definition of recovery ending when the lost packet that started recovery is acknowledged.

clauses.normalized_text: During recovery, the congestion window is not increased or decreased.
clauses.raw_text: During recovery, the congestion window is not increased or decreased.

clauses.normalized_text: As such, multiple lost packets only decrease the congestion window once as long as they’re lost before exiting recovery.
clauses.raw_text: As such, multiple lost packets only decrease the congestion window once as long as they’re lost before exiting recovery.

clauses.normalized_text: This causes QUIC to decrease the congestion window multiple times if retransmisions are lost, but limits the reduction to once per round trip.
clauses.raw_text: This causes QUIC to decrease the congestion window multiple times if retransmisions are lost, but limits the reduction to once per round trip.

clauses.normalized_text: If recovery sends a tail loss probe, no change is made to the congestion window or pacing rate.
clauses.raw_text: If recovery sends a tail loss probe, no change is made to the congestion window or pacing rate.

clauses.normalized_text: Acknowledgement or loss of tail loss probes are treated like any other packet.
clauses.raw_text: Acknowledgement or loss of tail loss probes are treated like any other packet.

clauses.normalized_text: When retransmissions are sent due to a retransmission timeout alarm, no change is made to the congestion window or pacing rate until the next acknowledgement arrives.
clauses.raw_text: When retransmissions are sent due to a retransmission timeout alarm, no change is made to the congestion window or pacing rate until the next acknowledgement arrives.

clauses.normalized_text: When an ack arrives, if packets prior to the first retransmission timeout are acknowledged, then the congestion window remains the same.
clauses.raw_text: When an ack arrives, if packets prior to the first retransmission timeout are acknowledged, then the congestion window remains the same.

clauses.normalized_text: If no packets prior to the first retransmission timeout are acknowledged, the retransmission timeout has been validated and the congestion window must be reduced to the minimum congestion window and slow start is begun.
clauses.raw_text: If no packets prior to the first retransmission timeout are acknowledged, the retransmission timeout has been validated and the congestion window must be reduced to the minimum congestion window and slow start is begun.

clauses.normalized_text: The pacing rate is a function of the mode, the congestion window, and the smoothed rtt.
clauses.raw_text: The pacing rate is a function of the mode, the congestion window, and the smoothed rtt.

clauses.normalized_text: Specifically, the pacing rate is 2 times the congestion window divided by the smoothed RTT during slow start and 1.25 times the congestion window divided by the smoothed RTT during congestion avoidance.
clauses.raw_text: Specifically, the pacing rate is 2 times the congestion window divided by the smoothed RTT during slow start and 1.25 times the congestion window divided by the smoothed RTT during congestion avoidance.

clauses.normalized_text: In order to fairly compete with flows that are not pacing, it is recommended to not pace the first 10 sent packets when exiting quiescence.
clauses.raw_text: In order to fairly compete with flows that are not pacing, it is recommended to not pace the first 10 sent packets when exiting quiescence.

clauses.normalized_text: bytes_in_flight:: The sum of the size in bytes of all sent packets that contain at least one retransmittable or PADDING frame, and have not been acked or declared lost.
clauses.raw_text: bytes_in_flight:: The sum of the size in bytes of all sent packets that contain at least one retransmittable or PADDING frame, and have not been acked or declared lost.

clauses.normalized_text: The size does not include IP or UDP overhead.
clauses.raw_text: The size does not include IP or UDP overhead.

clauses.normalized_text: Packets only containing ACK frames do not count towards byte_in_flight to ensure congestion control does not impede congestion feedback.
clauses.raw_text: Packets only containing ACK frames do not count towards byte_in_flight to ensure congestion control does not impede congestion feedback.

clauses.normalized_text: congestion_window:: Maximum number of bytes in flight that may be sent.
clauses.raw_text: congestion_window:: Maximum number of bytes in flight that may be sent.

clauses.normalized_text: end_of_recovery:: The largest packet number sent when QUIC detects a loss.
clauses.raw_text: end_of_recovery:: The largest packet number sent when QUIC detects a loss.

clauses.normalized_text: When a larger packet is acknowledged, QUIC exits recovery.
clauses.raw_text: When a larger packet is acknowledged, QUIC exits recovery.

clauses.normalized_text: ssthresh:: Slow start threshold in bytes.
clauses.raw_text: ssthresh:: Slow start threshold in bytes.

clauses.normalized_text: When the congestion window is below ssthresh, the mode is slow start and the window grows by the number of bytes acknowledged.
clauses.raw_text: When the congestion window is below ssthresh, the mode is slow start and the window grows by the number of bytes acknowledged.
